positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
I implemented an end-to-end deep learning algorithm to be used on Nest products. I built a training pipeline and a fully convolutional network using TensorFlow. I also ported the trained model onto the Edge TPU Dev Board for testing and evaluation. Then, I optimized the input pipeline and modified the model architecture for performance improvement, lower parameter size, and faster processing time.

Technologies and languages used: Python, TensorFlow, Google Borg

positions.title: Engineering Practicum Intern
positions.description:
The Google Hotels Ranking Team uses TensorFlow's deep learning to rank hotels for a given hotel search query. To serve users with better hotel results, I helped design and implement the following features:
- Trip type: Wrote program that backfills each trip type scores to training examples to perform offline analysis and save 2-3 weeks of data accumulation time.
- User price preference v2: Resolved flawed population of hotel price category and avoided training/serving skew.
- Web scores v2: Improved topicality matching for tail queries by adding multidimensional web signals.
- Time-related features: Increased signal coverage of booking window by passing user query time to ranking flow.

In addition to these features, I helped improve serving side robustness by creating monitoring dashboards for counting unknown critical features.

Technologies and languages used: C++, Python, Protocol Buffers, Google Borg

positions.title: Tutor
positions.description:
Kim & Jung Academy is a private academy that teaches a wide range of subjects, including English, math, and sciences, to students in K-12 grade. In this academy, students learn beyond the scope of what's taught in school, such as advanced algorithms for programming competitions.
Every weekend for two years, I tutored mathematics and computer science to students in middle school and high school in preparation for competitions such as American Mathematics Competition and USA Computing Olympiad.

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description:
MODD is a start-up IT company in Seoul, South Korea that specializes in developing beds that can alleviate insomnia through movement. The concept behind how bed movement can treat insomnia is similar to how rocking cribs induce better sleep for toddlers.
I participated in a research that studied which type of oscillation results in optimal sleep inducement. My primary task was to help write code for the oscillation control system of the bed frame, with the help from a mentor. I helped design a program that changes the oscillation direction, frequency, and intensity based on biomedical data input that tracks user's sleeping cycle and behavior. Although our research team did not find any correlations between oscillation frequency/intensity and sleep inducement, we were able to make a strong conclusion that vertical oscillations have a significantly stronger effect on inducing uninterrupted sleep than horizontal (sideways) oscillation.

projects.title: Personal Website Development
projects.description: I created my personal website from scratch, using HTML/CSS and JavaScript/jQuery. I also made my own online chess game and developed a chess AI. I am currently still working on designing better graphics/interfaces and improving my chess AI algorithm.

projects.title: Chess Robot with Visual Recognition
projects.description: This was a yearlong research project that I conducted during my senior year of high school. Although there are already a lot of chess robots developed, detection of chess pieces by computer vision has yet to be improved. Based on a research study by Danner and Kafafy from Stanford, I created an algorithm that uses weighted evaluations of multiple edge detection techniques to identify chess pieces. My code was written in Python using the OpenCV library.

organizations.name: UM Programming Team
organizations.description:
The UM Programming Team competes in the annual ACM International Collegiate Programming Contest, where college students are given the opportunity to demonstrate programming skills, problem-solving abilities, and teamwork.
Placed 2nd in Grand Valley Site for 2018 ACM ICPC East Central NA Regional.
